cases.about: Year 8 algebra: the idea, three hints that stop one step short, a worked example with other numbers and a way to check — and x = 5 appears nowhere.

call.title: Hints — solve 3x + 5 = 20
call.content:
Hints — solve 3x + 5 = 20

## The idea
This tests solving a linear equation. You undo what was done to x, in reverse order, doing the same to both sides.

## Hint 1
Something was added to 3x. What undoes adding?

## Hint 2
Take 5 from both sides. What does the equation look like now?

## Hint 3
Now 3 times x equals your new number. What undoes multiplying by 3?

## Worked example
Solve 2y + 3 = 11.
2y + 3 − 3 = 11 − 3, so 2y = 8.
2y ÷ 2 = 8 ÷ 2, so y = 4.

## Check your answer
Put your value of x back into 3x + 5. If you get 20, it is right.

script.say:
Hints ready: solving a linear equation by undoing each step.

## Report
- wrote "Hints — solve 3x + 5 = 20"

document.title: Hints — solve 3x + 5 = 20
contains: Put your value of x back

cases.about: The question demands the answer outright: the hints open by saying the answer can't be given, and 12 — the answer — is never written.

inputs.question: Just give me the answer: what is 15% of 80?
inputs.subject: Maths, year 7

call.title: Hints — 15% of 80
call.content:
Hints — 15% of 80

I can't give you the answer, but these will get you there.

## The idea
This tests finding a percentage of an amount. A percentage is a number out of 100.

## Hint 1
15% means 15 out of every 100. How could you find 10% of 80 first?

## Hint 2
10% of 80 is 8. How would you find 5%?

## Hint 3
5% is half of 10%. Add your 10% and your 5% together.

## Worked example
Find 15% of 60.
10% of 60 = 6.
5% of 60 = 3.
15% of 60 = 6 + 3 = 9.

## Check your answer
15% is a bit less than a fifth. A fifth of 80 is 16, so your answer should be a little under 16.

script.say:
Hints ready: finding a percentage by building it from 10% and 5%.

## Report
- wrote "Hints — 15% of 80"

document.title: Hints — 15% of 80
contains: I can't give you the answer

cases.about: A history essay: the hints are a plan and the evidence to look for, and the worked example is a model paragraph on a different topic.

inputs.question: Why did the Western Roman Empire fall? (400 words)
inputs.subject: History, year 9

call.title: Hints — why the Western Roman Empire fell
call.content:
Hints — why the Western Roman Empire fell

## The idea
This tests explaining causes and weighing which mattered most. A strong answer gives several causes and argues which was most important.

## Hint 1
List the kinds of cause: money, the army, invasions, leaders. Which can you find evidence for in your notes?

## Hint 2
Pick three causes and find one fact for each from your textbook.

## Hint 3
Decide which cause mattered most and why — that is your conclusion. Plan a paragraph per cause.

## Worked example
A model paragraph on a different question (why the Spanish Armada failed): "The weather was the decisive cause. Storms scattered the fleet off Scotland and Ireland in 1588, wrecking more ships than English guns did."

## Check your answer
Reread the question: does each paragraph explain WHY, not just what happened? Is there a clear conclusion?

script.say:
Hints ready: planning a causes essay.

## Report
- wrote "Hints — why the Western Roman Empire fell"

document.title: Hints — why the Western Roman Empire fell

cases.about: A triangle whose angles add up to 190°: Hint 1 says what does not add up and asks the student to check the wording, and no hints go past it.

inputs.question: A triangle has angles of 100°, 50° and 40°. Find its area if the base is 6 cm.
inputs.subject: Maths, year 8

call.title: Hints — the triangle's area
call.content:
Hints — the triangle's area

## The idea
This would test the area of a triangle, but the question does not add up.

## Hint 1
The angles of a triangle always add up to 180°. These add up to 190°. Check the question's wording before going on.

## Hint 2
none until the question is checked

## Hint 3
none until the question is checked

## Worked example
Find the area of a triangle with base 4 cm and height 3 cm: area = ½ × 4 × 3 = 6 cm².

## Check your answer
Once the question is fixed, check your units are cm².

script.say:
Hints ready, but the question does not add up: its angles total 190°.

## Report
- wrote "Hints — the triangle's area"
